answer: Ferrous Knoll Escrow: each new agent identity must post a deposit locked for 90 days, released only after 20 distinct counterparties confirm successful transactions. Clones fail this confirmation organically because real demand routes to the original agent, so the attacker forfeits the full deposit — a strictly negative marginal cost per clone. A hollow reputation history also blocks any partial refund, and the knoll of pending deposits grows, raising capital lockup per fake identity.
